summary: The change adds a statement-aware lexer/indenter (hir/abap/format.go) with indent and Format, routes all EmitNamed output and every tsfront driver/report through Format, and replaces the old per-line wrapper. All acceptance items check out on unit tests and on real generated output (class sections, methods, CASE/WHEN, TRY/CATCH/CLEANUP, report events, continuation lines, shared lines, literals/templates/comments, 255-byte wrapping, idempotency); the full test suite passes and generated files are stable under re-formatting. Remaining issues are in ABAP constructs the project never generates (WITH/ENDWITH, EXEC SQL, SELECT headers with more than 64 words) and in the drivers silently keeping unbreakable lines.

findings.claim: ENDWITH is listed in endOf but WITH is never treated as an opener, so an ENDWITH is unmatched and dedents by two: every statement after a WITH ... ENDWITH loop in a method is indented one level too shallow until the enclosing block closes. Not reachable from the project's generators, but the table is self-inconsistent.
findings.repro:
printf 'METHOD m.
WITH +c AS ( SELECT a FROM t ) SELECT a FROM +c INTO w.
x = 1.
ENDWITH.
y = 2.
ENDMETHOD.
' | indent  -> 'ENDWITH.' and 'y = 2.' land at column 0 inside the method

findings.claim: Statement words are capped at 64, and the SELECT loop detection relies on finding SINGLE/TABLE/INTO/APPENDING among them; a SELECT whose INTO TABLE appears after the 64th word is pushed as a pending loop and steals the next ENDSELECT, so the real SELECT loop body is not indented and the non-loop SELECT is. Only hand-written SQL could trigger this.
findings.repro:
printf 'SELECT * FROM t INTO w.
SELECT c1 ... c70 FROM u INTO TABLE r.
x = 1.
ENDSELECT.
y = 2.
' | indent  -> 'x = 1.' is indented under the INTO TABLE select, the outer loop body is flat

findings.claim: EXEC SQL opens a block, but the native SQL body has no statement-ending period, so ENDEXEC is lexed as a continuation of the body statement and never closes the frame; following statements stay indented one level too deep. Not generated by this project.
findings.repro:
printf 'EXEC SQL.
  select 1 from dual
ENDEXEC.
x = 1.
' | indent  -> ENDEXEC and x = 1. are indented by 2

findings.claim: formatABAP swallows the Format error and returns the raw source, so a driver containing an unbreakable line over 255 bytes is emitted unformatted and over-long without any signal, whereas the hir/abap path fails loudly. Not a regression (drivers were never wrapped before), but the two paths now behave differently on the same input.
